prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Summary of key proposals

Economy and taxes
- Eliminate the deficit, move to a budget surplus from 2018–19, and run surpluses in normal times; no rises in VAT, Income Tax or National Insurance.
- Raise the Personal Allowance to £12,500 and the higher-rate threshold to £50,000; link the allowance to the Minimum Wage (“tax-free minimum wage”).
- £30bn further fiscal consolidation via departmental savings, welfare savings, and tackling tax avoidance/evasion; continued crackdown on aggressive tax planning.
- Support challenger banks, ring-fence retail banking, maintain the bank levy, and promote fintech and SME finance (e.g., Help to Grow).

Jobs, business and skills
- Create 2 million more jobs and 3 million apprenticeships; aim for highest employment rate in the G7.
- Youth Allowance for 18–21s with stronger work/training requirements; restrict automatic Housing Benefit for this group.
- Cut £10bn more red tape; review business rates; expand Start Up Loans; 1/3 of central procurement to SMEs; permanent Office of Tax Simplification.
- Publish gender pay gap data for large employers; aim to halve the disability employment gap; enforce the Minimum Wage and curb exploitative practices.

Infrastructure and digital
- Over £100bn infrastructure plan: £38bn for rail (electrification, HS2/HS3, Crossrail 2), real-terms freeze of regulated rail fares, smart ticketing and better compensation.
- £15bn for roads, major upgrades and pothole funding; promote cycling and ultra-low emission vehicles.
- Superfast broadband to 95% by end-2017; ambition for ultrafast; expand mobile coverage to 90% of landmass and lead on 5G.

Housing and local growth
- Double first-time buyers vs previous five years; extend Help to Buy schemes and introduce a Help to Buy ISA (25% bonus).
- Build 200,000 Starter Homes (20% discount for under-40 first-time buyers); 275,000 additional affordable homes; 10,000 sub-market rental homes.
- Extend Right to Buy to Housing Association tenants with one-for-one replacements; prioritise brownfield, protect the Green Belt, support locally led garden towns.
- Devolve powers and budgets to city regions with elected mayors; allow councils to keep more business rates growth; keep council tax rises low via referendums.

Education and childcare
- Protect per-pupil funding; new literacy/numeracy standards; resits at secondary start if needed; EBacc subjects encouraged.
- Turn failing/coasting schools into academies; at least 500 new free schools; expand UTCs and degree apprenticeships.
- 30 hours’ free childcare for working parents of 3–4 year-olds; tax-free childcare up to £2,000 per child.

Health and social care
- Increase NHS spending each year; at least £8bn extra by 2020; implement the Five Year Forward View.
- Seven-day GP and hospital services by 2020; named GPs; same-day GP appointments for over-75s.
- Expand mental health access and waiting standards; sustain the Cancer Drugs Fund; faster access to innovative medicines; patient access to electronic records with opt-out.
- Integrate health and social care; cap residential care costs; increase dementia and carers’ support.

Welfare and poverty
- Overall welfare cap; two-year freeze of most working-age benefits from April 2016; reduce the household benefit cap to £23,000.
- Roll out Universal Credit; new measures addressing root causes of poverty; review benefit conditionality for treatable conditions with support to return to work.

Immigration
- Target net migration in the tens of thousands; reform EU welfare access (4-year contribution rule for tax credits/housing; end JSA for EU jobseekers).
- Stronger deportation and re-entry bans; extend “deport first, appeal later”; landlord checks; tackle illegal working; Controlling Migration Fund.
- English fluency requirement for public-facing roles; language progression for family visas.

Energy and environment
- Promote competition (smart meters by 2020); insulate 1 million more homes.
- Support shale gas with community benefits and a Northern Sovereign Wealth Fund; back new nuclear; end new subsidies for onshore wind and give locals final say.
- Meet climate commitments cost-effectively; expand offshore wind and low-carbon innovation.
- 25-year plan for nature; protect forests; 11 million more trees; stronger marine “Blue Belt”; more flood defences; tougher litter/fly-tipping penalties; animal welfare measures.

Crime, justice and security
- Continue police reform, transparency, technology use, and cyber capability; improve complaints system and diversity; targeted stop-and-search reforms.
- Ban new psychoactive substances; expand sobriety orders; modernise prisons and reduce contraband.
- Victims’ Law; stronger response to domestic abuse, FGM and child sexual exploitation.
- Replace the Human Rights Act with a British Bill of Rights; modernise courts; review legal aid.
- Update communications powers with oversight; new tools against non-violent extremism; tackle online radicalisation.

Pensions and older people
- Maintain the triple lock; introduce the single-tier pension; keep pensioner benefits.
- Cap care costs; no need to sell the home to fund residential care; greater freedom over pension savings and tax treatment.
- Raise the effective Inheritance Tax threshold for the family home to £1m for couples.

Constitution, EU and foreign policy
- English votes for English laws (including tax matters); implement new devolution for Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; boundary reforms and “votes for life” for expats.
- In–out EU referendum by end-2017 after a renegotiation; protect Single Market interests; seek repatriation of powers and end “ever closer union.”
- Maintain strong Armed Forces (minimum army 82,000), renew the nuclear deterrent, invest in equipment and reserves; uphold NATO commitments.
- Keep aid at 0.7% of GNI with outcomes on health, education, WASH, vaccines, girls’ rights and crisis response.

TEXT_D:
Summary of proposals (2015 manifesto)

Economy and public finances
- Raise the personal allowance to at least £13,000; lift the 40% threshold to £55,000; introduce a 30% intermediate band; abolish inheritance tax; expand transferable allowances for couples.
- Cut small business rates by 20% for properties with rateable value under £50,000.
- Reduce the deficit through: leaving the EU to save net contributions; lowering overseas aid to 0.2% of GNI; scrapping HS2; replacing the Barnett Formula with a needs-based system; streamlining government departments and quangos.
- Tougher action on multinational tax avoidance; restore UK tax sovereignty.

Immigration and borders
- End freedom of movement by leaving the EU; introduce an Australian-style points system; five-year moratorium on unskilled migration; limit skilled work visas to 50,000 annually.
- Increase Border Agency staff by 2,500; count entrants and exits; no amnesty for illegal immigration.
- Five-year qualifying period for most benefits and non-urgent NHS access; require health insurance for temporary migrants and students.
- Faster asylum processing; revoke citizenship obtained by fraud; deport foreign offenders.

NHS and social care
- Invest an extra £12bn over five years: 8,000 more GPs; 20,000 nurses; 3,000 midwives; GP-led triage in A&E; £1.5bn for mental health and dementia; free hospital parking.
- Create locally elected county health boards; introduce a “Licence to Manage” for NHS managers; end new PFI; exclude the NHS from TTIP; review EU directives affecting training/clinical trials.
- Increase social care funding by £1.2bn per year; integrate health and social care under the NHS; raise Carer’s Allowance; introduce a Dignity Code; improve home-care employment standards.

Welfare, pensions and families
- Scrap the “bedroom tax”; keep Housing Benefit for under-25s; crack down on fraud; replace ATOS-style assessments with GP/specialist-led process.
- Flexible state pension window; boost pensions guidance; criminalise pension cold-calling; restore war widows’ pensions for life.
- Maintain 15 free childcare hours; tax-free childcare; deregulate to expand childminding; require wrap-around school care 8am–6pm; shared parenting presumption; overhaul child protection.

Education
- Abolish Key Stage 1 SATs; reduce teacher workload; target class sizes of 25.
- Expand grammar, technical and vocational routes; later transfer exams; first-aid in PSHE.
- STEMM tuition fee waivers for UK students who work in-discipline in the UK for five years; reform Ofsted; limit EU student loan exposure post-EU exit.

Housing and environment
- Prioritise brownfield: national register, remediation grants, stamp duty relief on first sale; bring empty homes back into use; protect green belt; local referenda on major developments.
- Restrict access to social housing and Help to Buy to long-term taxpayers/citizens; reinvest Right to Buy receipts; homelessness register; allow inheritable mortgages.

Transport
- Cancel HS2; consider South East capacity after Airports Commission; reopen Manston Airport.
- Use speed cameras only for safety; remove road tolls where possible; oppose road-pricing tech; scrap DCPC; raise levy on foreign HGVs; VED exemption for 25+ year-old vehicles.

Energy
- Repeal the Climate Change Act; end new wind/solar subsidies (honour existing); support nuclear, gas, shale (with safeguards) and coal with CCS; abolish green levies and EU ETS participation; create a shale sovereign wealth fund.

Jobs and small business
- Prioritise domestic workers; enforce minimum wage; code for zero-hours (no exclusivity, notice/pay guarantees, path to secure contracts).
- Penalise large firms for systematic late payment; pilot state-backed trade credit insurance; 30 minutes free town-centre parking; simplify public procurement; reduce regulatory burdens.

Farming, food, and animal welfare
- UK Single Farm Payment (~£80/acre) capped; premiums for organic/rare breeds; support dairy co-ops; simplify sheep ID; clearer food labelling.
- Tougher sentences for cruelty; CCTV in abattoirs; ban live exports for slaughter; support small abattoirs.

Fishing
- Leave the CFP; establish 12-mile zone and 200-mile EEZ; protect under-10m fleet; end destructive methods; manage angling proportionately.

Heritage, pubs, and tourism
- Create a Minister for Heritage and Tourism; remove VAT on listed-building repairs; planning presumption for conservation; seaside regeneration; support pubs (micro-brewery tax breaks, optional ventilated smoking rooms), oppose minimum unit pricing.

Crime, justice, and policing
- Add 3,500 frontline police/prison staff; review constabulary structures; confirm UK Bill of Rights; withdraw from EU justice measures; decriminalise TV licence non-payment; reduce FOBT stakes; expand deportation of foreign offenders; focus prison education.

Political and local reform
- National referenda via citizen initiatives; robust recall; optional open primaries; committee veto powers on appointments/spending; proportional voting; tighten postal voting.
- Local binding referenda on major planning; weekly bins where desired; tackle antisocial behaviour; curb executive pay and waste.

Trade, defence, foreign aid, and EU exit
- Leave the EU via referendum; negotiate UK–EU free-trade access; regain WTO seat; pursue global FTAs and cooperation on shared issues.
- Spend at least 2% of GDP on defence; retain nuclear deterrent; strengthen carriers; create Director of National Intelligence; oppose an EU army; waive income tax for deployed personnel.
- Reduce overseas aid to ~0.2% of GNI; focus on emergency relief, health, water/sanitation; close DFID and merge functions into the Foreign Office; prioritise trade-led development.
